questions.q: What does the Grover oracle operator O do to the amplitude of a marked basis state |x⟩?
options: It measures the state immediately and collapses it to |x⟩
It flips its sign (multiplies by -1), leaving its magnitude -- and therefore its measurement probability -- unchanged
It doubles the magnitude of the marked amplitude
It sets the marked amplitude to exactly zero
questions.explain: O|x⟩ = (-1)^f(x)|x⟩ only changes sign for marked states (f(x)=1); the magnitude, and hence the probability if you measured right after the oracle alone, is unchanged.

questions.q: In terms of the amplitude vector a, what does one application of the diffusion operator D do to each entry a_i?
options: Replaces it with 2·mean(a) − a_i -- reflecting each amplitude about the average of all the amplitudes
Sets every entry equal to the mean, destroying all variation
questions.explain: D = 2|s⟩⟨s| − I works out, amplitude by amplitude, to new_a_i = 2·mean(a) − a_i -- exactly the 'reflect about the mean' arithmetic used in the chapter's verified examples.

questions.q: Geometrically, why does one oracle application followed by one diffusion application produce a net rotation of the state vector?
options: The oracle and diffusion operators are literally the same operation applied twice, which cancels out and does nothing
The angle of rotation grows larger with each iteration, so no two iterations rotate by the same amount
Rotation only happens if you measure the qubits between the oracle and the diffusion step
The oracle reflects the state about the unmarked-state axis, the diffusion operator reflects it about the starting-state axis, and two reflections compose into a single rotation by a fixed angle 2α
questions.explain: Two reflections in a 2D plane always compose into a rotation. Here the oracle reflects about the unmarked axis and diffusion reflects about the start-state axis, giving a rotation of exactly 2α per iteration, where sin(α)=1/√N.

questions.q: For N=4 with marked index 3, starting from [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5], what is the amplitude vector immediately after the oracle is applied, before diffusion?
questions.explain: The oracle only flips the sign of the marked index (index 3); the other three entries are untouched, giving [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, -0.5].

questions.q: Continuing that N=4 example, after the diffusion step is applied to [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, -0.5], what is the resulting amplitude vector and P(marked)?
questions.explain: The mean of [0.5,0.5,0.5,-0.5] is 0.25; applying new_a_i = 2(0.25) - a_i gives [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0], so P(marked) = 1.0² = 1.0 -- a deterministic success for this N=4 case.
